mainTopic: The מגדף's קרבן and כרת; which miscarriages require a יולדת's קרבן; and the night of the eighty-first day
overview: The amud opens by explaining רבי עקיבא's view that a מגדף who sinned by mistake brings a קרבן, because his כרת is written in the section about the חטאת. רבי עקיבא challenges the רבנן to explain why that כרת is written. They answer that it teaches כרת for the curser of ה׳, and through the words 'חטאו ישא' also for someone who skips פסח שני. Two ברייתות then show the argument over what a מגדף is: one who curses ה׳'s Name, or one who serves עבודה זרה. A new משנה sorts women after a miscarriage into three groups: those who bring a קרבן that is eaten, those who bring one that is not eaten because of a doubt, and those who bring none. The גמרא finds the source for including a שפחה. It then explains how two women can share a קרבן with a condition, and why רבי יוסי allows this for a מחוסר כפרה but not for a חטאת that comes for a sin. Next it gives the sources for רבי שמעון and the רבנן on a יוצא דופן birth. Finally, a new משנה records בית שמאי and בית הלל arguing about a miscarriage on the night of the eighty-first day.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the blasphemer brings an offering because his כרת is written next to the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's words: a מגדף brings a קרבן, because the Torah wrote his כרת inside the section about the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: a blasphemer brings an offering, because his כרת is written in the place where the Torah talks about an offering. These are רבי עקיבא's words. He holds: the Torah could have written כרת on its own, somewhere else. Since it wrote the כרת right in the offering section, we learn that he brings an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clears up what רבי עקיבא meant in the ברייתא: he holds that a מגדף who sinned by mistake brings a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lists the מגדף's כרת in במדבר 15:30, right after the laws of the חטאת offering for mistaken sins. רבי עקיבא reasons that this placement is no accident. If the Torah only wanted to give him כרת, it could have written it anywhere, so putting it in the offering section shows that he also brings a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A blasphemer, someone who speaks against ה׳
Being 'cut off', the heavenly punishment for certain serious sins done on purpose
An offering; here, the חטאת brought for a sin done by mistake
Since it should have / since it could have
In general, on its own, with no special connection

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
A blasphemer brings an offering
since כרת comes regarding him
in the place of an offering,
phrases.notes: The Torah mentions his כרת right in the section about the חטאת offering (במדבר 15:27–31).

phrases.english: these are the words of רבי עקיבא.
He holds: since it should have
written כרת in general,
and כרת is written in the place of an offering,
learn from it that he brings an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers an earlier question from the previous part of the daf by explaining what רבי עקיבא really means in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear what רבי עקיבא's statement in the ברייתא meant.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא holds a מגדף brings a קרבן, learned from where his כרת is written.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole argument: רבי עקיבא learns the קרבן from where the כרת is written, so the רבנן must explain that כרת some other way.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא challenges the רבנן: why is כרת written there at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the words 'ואומר חטאו ישא' as רבי עקיבא's challenge to the רבנן: if the מגדף does no action and brings no קרבן, what is the written כרת for?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it says: shall bear his sin.' Now we have come to the רבנן, and this is what רבי עקיבא is saying to them: You say a blasphemer has no action, because what is a blasphemer? Someone who 'blesses' (curses) ה׳'s Name. If so, the כרת that is written, what does it come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next part of the ברייתא. It is רבי עקיבא turning to the רבנן and asking them why the Torah wrote כרת for the מגדף, if in their view he brings no קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that a מגדף only speaks and does no physical מעשה, so he does not bring a חטאת. רבי עקיבא attacks this: according to him, the כרת in במדבר 15:30 is there to teach the קרבן. If the רבנן deny the קרבן, that כרת seems to have no purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: A physical action; the רבנן hold a חטאת comes only for a sin with an action
Literally 'blesses the Name', a polite way of saying cursing ה׳
For what does it come? What is it teaching?
And it says; brings another פסוק to back up a point

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'מברך את השם' as truly blessing. It is a polite way of writing 'cursing'; the גמרא avoids writing the ugly words directly.

phrases.english: And it says: "shall bear his sin."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:15

phrases.english: We have arrived at the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: The ן in square brackets is the corrected wording, so read it as 'we have arrived.' רבי עקיבא now turns to challenge the רבנן.

phrases.english: and this is what רבי עקיבא is saying to the Rabbis:
You say a blasphemer has no action in it,
what is a blasphemer? One who 'blesses' the Name.
But the כרת that is written,
phrases.notes: He means the כרת in במדבר 15:30, right after the offering section.

phrases.english: for what does it come?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 1: since רבי עקיבא uses the written כרת to prove a קרבן, he asks the רבנן what that כרת is for in their view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that a מגדף brings no קרבן because he does no action
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מגדף brings no קרבן, the כרת written in the offering section seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: The רבנן answer: the כרת teaches about the curser and about פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן reply that the כרת is written to teach that a מקלל gets כרת, and from there we learn by comparing the words 'חטאו ישא' that someone who skips פסח שני also gets כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: it comes to give כרת to the curser. About the curser it is written 'he shall bear his sin', and about פסח שני it is written 'shall bear his sin'. Just as there it means כרת, so too here it means כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן answer רבי עקיבא's question: the written כרת has a different job, not teaching a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כרת in במדבר 15:30 tells us that 'נשא חטאו' said about the מקלל in ויקרא 24:15 means כרת. Then, since פסח שני uses the same words 'חטאו ישא' (במדבר 9:13), we learn that skipping פסח שני is also punished with כרת. So the כרת has a purpose, and there is no proof for a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: One who curses (here, curses ה׳)
The second פסח, a month later, for those who could not bring the קרבן פסח on time
He shall bear his sin; the shared words used for the comparison
Just as there... so too here; the form of a word-comparison (גזירה שוה)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן avoid רבי עקיבא's proof by giving the written כרת another job: it defines 'חטאו ישא' as כרת, which then teaches כרת for skipping פסח שני.

phrases.english: They said to him: to give כרת to one who curses,
as it is written regarding one who curses:
"he shall bear his sin,"
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets, but the corrected text leaves them out. The words in square brackets are the right wording of ויקרא 24:15.

phrases.english: and it is written regarding the second Pesach: "shall bear his sin,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 9:13

phrases.english: just as there, it means כרת,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the curser, whose punishment we know is כרת.

phrases.english: so too here, it means כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי עקיבא's challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the verse a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The written כרת seems useless unless it teaches a קרבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כרת teaches that the curser gets כרת, which lets us learn כרת for פסח שני through the shared words 'חטאו ישא'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for the rule that someone who deliberately skips פסח שני is punished with כרת.

steps.title: איסי בן יהודה explains the word מגדף
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings איסי בן יהודה's explanation that מגדף is like 'scraping the bowl and making it lacking', showing he holds a מגדף is one who curses ה׳'s Name.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'he blasphemes ה׳‎'. איסי בן יהודה says: this is like a person who says to his friend, 'You scraped the bowl clean and made it lacking.' He holds: a מגדף is one who 'blesses' (curses) the Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the meaning of the word מגדף in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בן יהודה connects מגדף to the similar-sounding word גירף, 'scraping'. Cursing ה׳ is so serious it is like taking something away from Him, like scraping a bowl until it is empty. The גמרא concludes that he understands מגדף as the actual curser of ה׳'s Name.

keyTerms.meaning: You scraped (clean); sounds like מגדף
A bowl
You made it lacking
He holds; the גמרא explaining the view behind a statement

steps.whatToRemember: According to איסי בן יהודה, מגדף means cursing ה׳'s Name, a very serious sin, compared to scraping a bowl empty.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "He blasphemes ה׳,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:30

phrases.english: איסי בן יהודה says:
Like a person who says to his friend:
"You scraped the bowl and made it lacking."
phrases.notes: A play on words: גירפת (scraped) sounds like מגדף.

phrases.english: He holds: a blasphemer
is one who 'blesses' the Name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ברייתא that defines the word מגדף, which was discussed in steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: איסי בן יהודה holds that מגדף means one who curses ה׳'s Name.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's picture of the scraped bowl
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה compares the מגדף to someone who scraped a bowl but did not make it lacking. The גמרא explains that he holds a מגדף is one who serves עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: it is like a person who tells his friend, 'You scraped the bowl, but you did not make it lacking.' The גמרא explains: he holds that a מגדף is the same as someone who serves עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now gives a second view on the word מגדף. The גמרא explains what this view tells us about who a מגדף is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איסי בן יהודה said the bowl was scraped AND made lacking, which fits someone who curses ה׳ directly. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it was NOT made lacking. So for him, the מגדף does not attack ה׳ directly. That is why the גמרא says that for him a מגדף is someone who serves עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The person the Torah calls a blasphemer; the question here is what exactly he did
You scraped the bowl clean
You did not make it lacking or damaged
He holds; this introduces the reasoning behind someone's view
Someone who serves idols

steps.confusionAlert: The two pictures sound almost the same, but the difference is the key. איסי says the bowl WAS made lacking, so the מגדף curses ה׳‎. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it was NOT made lacking, so the מגדף serves עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
It is like a person who says to his friend:
'You scraped the bowl, but you did not make it lacking.'

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: מְגַדֵּף – הַיְינוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: He holds: a מגדף is the same as one who serves עבודה זרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: כְּאָדָם הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposing view to איסי בן יהודה's explanation in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a מגדף is someone who serves עבודה זרה. He is not someone who curses ה׳'s Name.

steps.title: Another ברייתא states the argument openly
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא shows the same argument clearly. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the פסוק is about עבודה זרה. The חכמים say it gives כרת to someone who curses ה׳'s Name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: about the words 'את ה׳', רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the פסוק is speaking about someone who serves עבודה זרה. The חכמים say the פסוק only comes to give כרת to someone who 'blesses' (meaning curses) ה׳'s Name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא. It openly states the argument that the גמרא just worked out from the picture of the bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, the גמרא worked out רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view from his picture (קסבר). Here a ברייתא says the same thing directly, so it supports that reading. It also shows that the חכמים agree with איסי: the פסוק is about cursing ה׳'s Name.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק is speaking about
The פסוק comes only to teach...
A punishment from Heaven of being cut off
Literally 'blesses the Name'; a polite way of saying 'curses ה׳'s Name'

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about the מגדף: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says he serves עבודה זרה. איסי and the חכמים say he curses ה׳'s Name.

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
'Hashem' (from the פסוק about the מגדף).
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:30

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
The פסוק is speaking about one who serves עבודה זרה.
And the חכמים say:
The פסוק comes only
to give כרת to one who 'blesses' the Name.
phrases.notes: 'Blesses' is a polite way of saying 'curses.' The גמרא avoids writing the harsh word about ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This confirms, in plain words, the view the גמרא worked out in Step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds a מגדף is someone who serves עבודה זרה, and that the חכמים hold he curses ה׳'s Name.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא explaining the words 'את ה׳'.

steps.title: New משנה: three groups of women and their קרבן
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה sorts women into three groups. Some bring a קרבן that is eaten, some bring a קרבן that is not eaten, and some bring no קרבן at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Some women bring a קרבן and it is eaten. Some bring a קרבן and it is not eaten. And some do not bring one at all.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and lists three groups as a heading. It is setting up the details that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the general outline. The משנה will now go through each group one by one. The first group is a woman who brings a קרבן that the כהנים eat.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
An offering brought in the בית המקדש
It is eaten (by the כהנים)

phrases.english: משנה:
There are women who bring a קרבן, and it is eaten,
and there are women who bring a קרבן, and it is not eaten,
and there are women who do not bring one at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A brand-new topic. The discussion of the מגדף is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women fall into three groups: a קרבן that is eaten, a קרבן that is not eaten, and no קרבן at all.

steps.title: A miscarriage shaped like an animal: רבי מאיר versus the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The first group is a woman who miscarries a fetus shaped like an animal or a bird. רבי מאיר says she brings a קרבן that is eaten. The חכמים say she brings one only if the fetus has a human form.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women who bring a קרבן that is eaten: a woman who miscarries something shaped like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird. This is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say she does not bring one unless it has a human form.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts filling in the first group. It gives an example, and רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר counts a fetus shaped like an animal or bird as a real birth, so the woman brings a קרבן. The חכמים say only a fetus with some human form counts. So for them, the animal-shaped miscarriage does not make her bring one.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries
A domestic animal
A wild animal
A bird
A human form

phrases.english: Those who bring a קרבן and it is eaten:
A woman who miscarries something shaped like a domestic animal, a wild animal, or a bird,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the חכמים say:
Not unless it has some human form.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְבִיאוֹת קׇרְבָּן וְנֶאֱכָל: הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה חַיָּה וָעוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This explains the first group from the heading in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a miscarriage shaped like an animal or bird brings a קרבן that is eaten. חכמים: only if it has a human form.

steps.title: More cases where the woman brings a קרבן that is eaten
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds more cases to the first group: a סנדל-shaped fetus, a שליא, a שפיר מרוקם, a fetus that came out in pieces, and a שפחה who miscarried. All bring a קרבן that is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who miscarries a fetus shaped like a flat fish, or an afterbirth, or a sac with formed tissue, or a fetus that came out in pieces, and also a maidservant who miscarried, brings a קרבן, and it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing cases in the first group, the women who bring a קרבן that the כהנים eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these cases counts as a real birth, even though the baby did not come out whole or normal. So the woman is definitely obligated, and her קרבן is a proper one that may be eaten. The שפחה is added to show that she is included in these laws too.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus shaped like a flat fish
The afterbirth (placenta)
A sac in which body tissue has formed
A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew

phrases.english: A woman who miscarries a sandal-shaped fetus
phrases.notes: A סנדל is a fetus shaped like a flat fish.

phrases.english: or an afterbirth
or a sac with formed tissue,
or a fetus that comes out cut into pieces,
and likewise a maidservant who miscarried,
brings a sacrifice, and it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the first group of the משנה, the women whose קרבן is eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סנדל, a שליא, a שפיר מרוקם, a fetus that came out in pieces, and a שפחה's miscarriage all obligate a קרבן that is eaten.

steps.title: Women who bring a קרבן that is not eaten
steps.stepSummary: The second group: a woman who does not know what she miscarried, and two women where only one of them miscarried something that obligates a קרבן. They bring a קרבן, but it is not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: These women bring a קרבן, but it is not eaten: a woman who miscarried and does not know what it was, and two women who miscarried, where one miscarried a type that is exempt and the other a type that obligates.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to its second group: women who bring a קרבן because of a doubt, but the קרבן cannot be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these cases we do not know whether this woman is really obligated. She brings the קרבן to be safe. But since maybe she was never obligated, it might not be a real קרבן, so the כהנים may not eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of miscarriage that does not require a קרבן
A type of miscarriage that does require a קרבן
Their קרבנות are not eaten

steps.confusionAlert: With the two women, each one brings her own קרבן, and neither is eaten, because for each woman on her own it is a doubt.

phrases.english: And these bring, but their sacrifices are not eaten:
a woman who miscarries and does not know what she miscarried,
and two women who miscarried,
one a type that is exempt
and one a type that obligates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first group to the second group announced in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When it is a doubt whether she is obligated, she brings a קרבן, but it is not eaten.

steps.title: רבי יוסי limits the two-women case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the two women's קרבנות are not eaten only when they went off separately. If they stand together, they bring one shared קרבן, and it is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: When is this? When they went off, one to the east and one to the west. But if both were standing together, both bring one קרבן, and it is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי narrows the rule of the two women from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Apart, each woman is a doubt, so neither קרבן can be eaten. Together, it is certain that one of the two is obligated. So one shared קרבן, brought for whichever woman owes it, is a real קרבן and may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: When? A word that introduces a limit on a rule
East and west, meaning they went off separately

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: When is this?
When they went off,
this one to the east and that one to the west.
But if both of them were standing together,
both of them bring one sacrifice, and it is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the two-women case from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the two women are together, they bring one shared קרבן, and it is eaten.

steps.title: Women who bring no קרבן, and רבי שמעון's view on יוצא דופן
steps.stepSummary: The third group brings no קרבן: a sac with only water, blood, or colored matter; a fetus shaped like fish or creeping things; a miscarriage on the fortieth day; and יוצא דופן. רבי שמעון obligates a קרבן for יוצא דופן.
steps.simpleTranslation: These do not bring a קרבן: a woman who miscarries a sac full of water, blood, or colored matter; one who miscarries something like fish, grasshoppers, or creeping creatures; one who miscarries on the fortieth day; and a baby born through the side. רבי שמעון obligates her for a baby born through the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third group, the women who do not bring any קרבן, and records רבי שמעון's disagreement about one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these count as a birth for this law. There is no formed fetus, or the form is not one that counts, or it is too early in the pregnancy. For יוצא דופן the baby is real, but it was not born the normal way. The first opinion exempts her, and רבי שמעון obligates her.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born through the side (a caesarean birth)
Different-colored matter with no form
The fortieth day of pregnancy, too early to count as a birth
Repulsive creatures and creeping things
Obligates (requires a קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: Three groups: (1) a real birth, so the קרבן is eaten; (2) a doubt, so she brings one but it is not eaten; (3) not a birth, so no קרבן. רבי שמעון obligates for יוצא דופן.

phrases.english: These do not bring a sacrifice:
a woman who miscarries a sac full of water,
full of blood, or full of colored matter,
a woman who miscarries something like fish or grasshoppers
or repulsive creatures or creeping things,
a woman who miscarries on the fortieth day,
and a baby born through the side.
phrases.notes: Literally 'goes out the wall,' meaning a caesarean birth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon obligates her in the case of a baby born through the side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the three groups announced in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These cases bring no קרבן; רבי שמעון disagrees about יוצא דופן.

steps.title: How do we know a שפחה brings a קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that a שפחה who miscarries brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How do we know that a maidservant is included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a question: where does the משנה's rule about a שפחה come from? It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to בני ישראל, and a שפחה is not a full Jewish woman. So it is not obvious that she is included in this law, and the גמרא asks for a source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: A maidservant, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the שפחה from step 9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by asking for the source of a detail in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a שפחה is obligated in the קרבן of a woman after birth.

steps.title: The word ״אשה״ includes a convert and a שפחה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says ״בני ישראל״ alone would mean only Jewish women, but the extra word ״אשה״ includes a גיורת and a שפחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: "The children of Israel" would give me only the children of Israel. From where do I know a convert and a maidservant? The פסוק says "a woman."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא that learns from the word ״אִשָּׁה״ in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, ״בני ישראל״ would limit the law to women born Jewish. The extra word ״אשה״ widens the law to include a גיורת and a שפחה, and that is the source for the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (this narrow case)
A woman who converted to Judaism
The פסוק teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A שפחה is included in the קרבן after birth because of the word ״אשה״ in ויקרא 12:2.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"The children of Israel":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2

phrases.english: I would have only the children of Israel.
From where do I know a convert and a maidservant?
The verse says: "a woman."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״אשה״ in the פסוק includes a גיורת and a שפחה.

steps.title: Why does the משנה add 'and likewise a שפחה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to add the words 'and likewise a שפחה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of saying 'and likewise a שפחה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothered to mention a שפחה with the special words 'and likewise'. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 already showed from a ברייתא that a שפחה brings a קרבן. Now the גמרא asks a different question: why did the משנה think it needed to say this outright? It seems obvious, so there must be a reason we might have thought otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew, who keeps some מצוות
And likewise; the same rule applies here too

phrases.english: What is the point of 'and likewise a maidservant'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding the source for the שפחה rule, the גמרא asks why the משנה needed to state it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה found it necessary to say 'and likewise a שפחה', since it seems obvious.

steps.title: A יולדת's קרבן is only for women, so the שפחה needed saying
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the slave rule only covers laws shared by men and women, so the משנה had to teach that a שפחה also brings a יולדת's קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: when we say 'any מצוה a woman must keep, a slave must keep too,' that only applies to a law that is the same for men and women. But a יולדת's קרבן applies only to women and not to men, so you might say a שפחה is not obligated. That is why the משנה taught 'שפחה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that without the משנה's words, we might have exempted a שפחה from a יולדת's קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a slave keeps every מצוה a woman keeps. But you could limit that rule to מצוות that apply to both men and women. A יולדת's קרבן applies only to women, so the משנה had to say outright that a שפחה brings it too.

keyTerms.meaning: It might enter your mind to say: the first, mistaken thought
A non-Jewish slave owned by a Jew
This statement applies only to...
A woman who has given birth, who must bring קרבנות
For this reason the משנה taught it

steps.confusionAlert: The rule 'a slave keeps what a woman keeps' is about male slaves too. The fear was not that a שפחה is unlike a woman, but that the rule might only cover laws shared by both men and women.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
When we say: any מצוה
that a woman is obligated in,
a slave is obligated in it,
that applies only to something
that is the same for a man and for a woman.
But a woman after childbirth, which exists among women,
but does not exist among men,
I might say a maidservant is not obligated,
so for this reason it taught: maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the משנה mentioned a שפחה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without the משנה, we would have limited the slave rule to laws shared by men and women, and exempted a שפחה from a יולדת's קרבן, which applies only to women.

steps.title: How do the two women bring one shared קרבן?
steps.stepSummary: Turning to רבי יוסי's case in the משנה, the גמרא asks how exactly two women bring one shared קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'These bring a קרבן,' and so on. What exactly do they do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of two women, where רבי יוסי said they can bring one shared קרבן. It asks how this actually works, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the two women is really obligated, but nobody knows which one. The question is practical: how can one קרבן work for two women when only one of them owes it?

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do? How does it work in practice?

phrases.english: These bring an offering, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה; the 'etc.' points to רבי יוסי's case of two women standing together, from step 11.

phrases.english: What do they do?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן כּוּ׳. מַאי עָבְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שפחה topic and opens a new question on רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical method by which two women, only one of whom is obligated, bring one shared קרבן.

steps.title: One definite קרבן, one doubtful bird חטאת, and a condition
steps.stepSummary: The two women bring one definite קרבן together, plus a bird חטאת brought out of doubt, and they make a condition about whose it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two of them bring one definite קרבן, and a bird חטאת because of the doubt, and they make a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the method: the two women share the קרבנות and make a condition about who owns them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the two women surely owes the יולדת's offerings, so one definite קרבן (the עולה) is brought. The bird חטאת is brought out of doubt, since we don't know whose it is. The condition means each קרבן belongs to whichever woman is really obligated.

keyTerms.meaning: A definite קרבן, brought because the obligation is certain
A חטאת offering brought from a bird
Doubt; brought because we are not sure
They make a condition

phrases.english: The two of them bring
one definite offering,
and a bird sin offering out of doubt,
and they make a condition.
phrases.notes: The condition means each woman says: if I am the one obligated, this is mine; if not, it belongs to the other woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how the shared קרבן works.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They bring one definite קרבן and one bird חטאת out of doubt, together, with a condition that it belongs to whoever is truly obligated.

steps.title: But elsewhere רבי יוסי does not allow a condition for a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: in another משנה, רבי יוסי says two people cannot bring one shared חטאת, which shows he does not accept a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really accept a condition? But we learned in a משנה: רבי שמעון says the two of them bring one חטאת together. רבי יוסי says they do not bring one חטאת together. So it seems רבי יוסי does not accept a condition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 18 by pointing to another משנה where רבי יוסי rejects a shared חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared קרבן in step 18 works only through a condition. But in another case of two people where one owes a חטאת, רבי יוסי says they may not share one. That suggests he does not let a condition work for a חטאת, so how can he allow it here?

keyTerms.meaning: A condition; making the קרבן belong to whoever is truly obligated
One single חטאת offering shared by two people
Evidently; so we see that

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי תְּנָאָה?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei accept a condition?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
Rabbi Shimon says:
The two of them bring one sin offering.
Rabbi Yosei says
the two of them do not bring one sin offering.
Evidently, Rabbi Yosei
does not accept a condition!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי תְּנָאָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method in step 18 as clashing with רבי יוסי's view elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי lets the two women share a קרבן through a condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In another משנה רבי יוסי forbids two people from sharing one חטאת, showing he rejects a condition for a חטאת, which contradicts his ruling here.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees in the case of a מחוסר כפרה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי יוסי agrees a condition works for a מחוסר כפרה, and רבין reports the same from רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי יוסי agrees in the case of a מחוסר כפרה. And likewise, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: רבי יוסי agrees in the case of a מחוסר כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by showing the two cases are different. Then the גמרא adds that רבי יוחנן said the exact same thing, as reported by רבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת is a מחוסר כפרה: she still needs her קרבן to finish her purification. In that kind of case רבי יוסי agrees that a condition works. The other משנה was a plain חטאת for a sin, where he does not allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees; admits this case is different
Someone still missing their atonement קרבן to complete purification, like a יולדת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי usually does not let two people share a חטאת by condition, but he agrees it works for a מחוסר כפרה like a יולדת. That is why the two women in the משנה can share a קרבן.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean רבי יוסי changed his mind. He still rejects a shared חטאת in the other case; the מחוסר כפרה case is an exception.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rabbi Yosei agrees in the case of one lacking atonement.
phrases.notes: A יולדת can't fully finish her purification until her קרבן is brought, so she is 'lacking atonement.'

phrases.english: And likewise, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Rabbi Yosei agrees in the case of one lacking atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בִּמְחוּסַּר כַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by limiting רבי יוסי's rejection of conditions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a מחוסר כפרה is an exception to רבי יוסי's usual view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי never lets a condition work for a shared חטאת, so the women could not share a קרבן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי rejects conditions for an ordinary חטאת for a sin, but agrees they work for a מחוסר כפרה like a יולדת, as both רבא and רבי יוחנן say.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains how רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה fits with his view elsewhere, and shows a יולדת's קרבן is treated differently from a regular חטאת.

steps.title: Why does a condition work here but not for a regular חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the difference רבא just made.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a condition works for a מחוסר כפרה but not for a חטאת brought for a sin. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20 רבא said רבי יוסי accepts a condition for a מחוסר כפרה. Now the גמרא wants the logic: why should the two kinds of קרבן be treated differently?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why does a condition help a woman who needs atonement, but not someone bringing a חטאת for a sin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's distinction in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a condition works for a מחוסר כפרה but not for a sin-חטאת.

steps.title: A sin-offering needs knowledge, a יולדת's offering does not
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת for a sin needs the sinner to know he sinned, so a condition cannot work. A יולדת brings her קרבן only to be allowed to eat קדשים, so a condition is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the person needs to know about his sin, as the פסוק says 'or his sin be made known to him.' So two people cannot bring one together with a condition. But here, women bring their קרבן only so they may eat קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A regular חטאת needs clear knowledge of the sin, but a יולדת's קרבן is about becoming allowed to eat holy food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a condition, nobody knows for sure who sinned, and a חטאת for a sin needs ידיעה, so it fails. A woman after birth did not sin; her קרבן only finishes her purification so she can eat קדשים. Not knowing which woman the קרבן belongs to does not cause a problem there.

keyTerms.meaning: Clear knowledge that one sinned
They make a condition
To become permitted
Eating sacred (offering) food

steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת for a sin needs ידיעה, so a condition fails. A קרבן that only makes someone allowed to eat קדשים can be brought with a condition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic difference between a קרבן that atones for a sin and a קרבן that only finishes a person's purification.

phrases.english: There, the man needs knowledge,
phrases.notes: "There" means a regular חטאת brought for a sin.

phrases.english: as it is written: "Or his sin be made known to him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:28

phrases.english: Therefore, they do not bring it together and make a condition.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, כִּי מַתְיָין נָשִׁים קׇרְבָּן
phrases.english: But here, when women bring a קרבן,
it is to become permitted to eat sacred food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A sin-חטאת needs ידיעה, so a condition fails. A יולדת's קרבן only lets her eat קדשים, so a condition works.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's own words limit his rule to a חטאת for a sin
steps.stepSummary: The end of that same משנה quotes רבי יוסי: two people cannot share any חטאת that comes for a sin. This means a חטאת that is not for a sin can be shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught at the end of that משנה: רבי יוסי says, any חטאת that comes for a sin, two people cannot bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from רבי יוסי's own wording. He only forbids sharing a חטאת that comes for a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's words 'that comes for a sin' show his rule has a limit. A יולדת's חטאת does not come for a sin, so two women may share it with a condition. This fits the answer of step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
A חטאת brought to atone for a sin

phrases.english: As is taught in the last clause of that one:
phrases.notes: "That one" is the משנה quoted in step 19.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל חַטָּאת שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה עַל חֵטְא
phrases.english: Any חטאת that comes for a sin,
two people do not bring it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 22 with רבי יוסי's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי's ban on a condition applies only to a חטאת that atones for a sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last clause of the משנה quoted in step 19, where רבי יוסי says 'any חטאת that comes for a sin.'

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון obligate a יוצא דופן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה: רבי שמעון obligates a woman who gave birth by caesarean to bring a קרבן. It asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'These women do not bring a קרבן, etc.' רבי שמעון obligates a woman in a case of יוצא דופן. What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה and asks for רבי שמעון's source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists women who do not bring a קרבן, and one of them gave birth by יוצא דופן. רבי שמעון disagrees and obligates her. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק he learns this from.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born through the side of the body (caesarean birth)
He obligates

phrases.english: "These do not bring, etc."
Rabbi Shimon obligates in a case of a caesarean birth.
What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבי יוסי and opens a new section on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי שמעון's ruling that a יוצא דופן birth requires a קרבן.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: "she bears" includes another kind of birth
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the word 'תלד' in the פסוק adds another kind of birth, and that is יוצא דופן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the פסוק says 'And if she bears a girl.' This comes to include another kind of birth. Which one? A caesarean birth.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives רבי שמעון's source. The extra word 'תלד' adds a different kind of birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already speaks about a woman giving birth, so saying 'תלד' again looks extra. רבי שמעון learns from this extra word that one more kind of birth counts, and the only one left is יוצא דופן.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (learned from an extra word)
Another kind of birth

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The verse says: "And if she bears a girl,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:5

phrases.english: to include another kind of birth.
What is it? A caesarean birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'תלד' in ויקרא 12:5 includes another kind of birth, which is יוצא דופן.

steps.title: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן exempt a יוצא דופן birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what is their reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks for the other side's source. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After hearing רבי שמעון's source, we need to know where the רבנן learn that a caesarean birth does not need a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what is their reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי שמעון's source, asks for the רבנן's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the רבנן's ruling that a יוצא דופן birth is exempt.

steps.title: רבי מני בר פטיש: the birth must come from where she conceived
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links giving birth to 'תזריע' (conceiving). So the laws apply only when she gives birth from the same place where she conceived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני בר פטיש said: 'A woman who conceives and gives birth' means only when she gives birth from the place where she conceives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני בר פטיש gives the רבנן's source from the start of the פרשה. A caesarean birth is not from the place of conception, so these laws do not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins 'תזריע' and 'וילדה'. The רבנן learn that the birth has to come from the same place as the conception. A יוצא דופן birth comes out through the side, so it is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: She conceives (receives seed)
The place where she conceives (the normal birth canal)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון includes a יוצא דופן birth from the word 'תלד'. The רבנן exclude it from 'תזריע וילדה', since the birth must come from the place of conception.

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani bar Pattish said:
"A woman who conceives and gives birth"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:2

phrases.english: only when she gives birth from the place where she conceives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'אשה כי תזריע וילדה' (ויקרא 12:2), the birth must come from the place of conception, which leaves out יוצא דופן.

steps.title: The new משנה: miscarriage on the night of the eighty-first day
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי exempt a woman who miscarries on the night of day 81 from a new קרבן. בית הלל obligate her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who miscarries on the night before the eighty-first day: בית שמאי exempt her from the קרבן, and בית הלל obligate her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל. The question is whether a miscarriage on the night that starts day 81 needs its own קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Births during the first 80 days are covered by the קרבן she brings on day 81. The night of day 81 is in between: it is already day 81, but a קרבן cannot be brought at night. בית שמאי treat that night as still covered by the old period, so no new קרבן is needed. בית הלל treat it as a new birth that needs its own קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה being studied
A woman who miscarries
On the night before (literally 'at the light of')
They exempt
They obligate

steps.confusionAlert: 'לְאוֹר' sounds like 'light' or daytime. Here it means the night that begins day 81, before the morning comes.

phrases.english: MISHNA
A woman who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first [day]
Beit Shammai exempt [her] from the offering
and Beit Hillel obligate [her].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of יוצא דופן ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Night of day 81: בית שמאי exempt her from a new קרבן, and בית הלל obligate her.

steps.title: בית הלל argue that the night and the day should be equal
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל ask: if the night of day 81 equals the day for טומאה, why not for the קרבן too?
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: What is the difference between the night of day 81 and the day of day 81? If they are the same for טומאה, should they not be the same for the קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל challenge בית שמאי's position. They point out that the night of day 81 already counts as day 81 for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the night of day 81 her blood already makes her טמאה, just as it would during the day. So the night has left the old protected period. בית הלל argue that if the night belongs to the new period for טומאה, it should also belong to it for the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
It was equal or the same
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
What is different about the night of the eighty-first
from the day of the eighty-first?
If it is equal to it regarding impurity,
phrases.notes: Blood she sees on that night already makes her טמאה, just like blood on the day itself.

phrases.english: should it not be equal to it regarding the offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא אוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד מִיּוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית הלל attack בית שמאי's ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's exemption for a miscarriage on the night of day 81
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The night already equals the day for טומאה, so it should also equal the day for the קרבן.

steps.title: בית שמאי: only the day is fit for bringing a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי explain the difference: the day of day 81 is a time when a קרבן can be brought, but the night is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: No. You may say this about a woman who miscarries on the day of day 81, because she has entered a time when she can bring a קרבן. Would you say the same about a woman who miscarries on the night of day 81, when she has not entered a time when she can bring a קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי defend their ruling. They point to a real difference between the night and the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי agree that the night equals the day for טומאה. But a קרבן is not brought at night. On the day, she has reached the point where she can bring her קרבן, so a new birth starts a new obligation. At night she has not yet reached that point, so the miscarriage still falls under the old period.

keyTerms.meaning: Because, since
She has entered a time period
Fit, suitable

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד
phrases.english: No. If you said [this] about one who miscarries on the eighty-first day,
that is because she has entered a time
in which she is fit to bring an offering.
Would you say [the same] about one who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first,
where she has not entered a time
in which she is fit to bring an offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בְּמַפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית הלל's comparison by showing a difference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The night of day 81 equals the day in every way, as it does for טומאה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the קרבן, what matters is reaching a time fit for bringing it, and the night is not such a time.

steps.title: בית הלל's counterexample: day 81 on שבת
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל point to day 81 falling on שבת. A קרבן cannot be brought then, yet a miscarriage that day still obligates her.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: But a woman who miscarries on day 81 when it falls on שבת proves the point. She has not entered a time when she can bring a קרבן, yet she must bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל reject בית שמאי's distinction with a counterexample. They show a case where she cannot bring a קרבן, yet she is still obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual's קרבן is not brought on שבת. So on a שבת that is day 81, she also has not reached a time fit for bringing a קרבן, just like at night. Everyone agrees she is obligated in that case. So 'fit to bring a קרבן' cannot be the deciding factor.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not so
Will prove, will show
That happens to fall on

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי tie the new obligation to having reached a time fit for bringing a קרבן. בית הלל answer that day 81 on שבת is not such a time, yet it still obligates her.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
But one who miscarries on the eighty-first day
that falls on Shabbat will prove [otherwise],
for she has not entered a time
in which she is fit to bring an offering,
and yet she is obligated in an offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא הַמַּפֶּלֶת יוֹם שְׁמוֹנִים וְאֶחָד שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת תּוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks בית שמאי's distinction with a counterexample.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's rule that the obligation depends on reaching a time fit for bringing a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Day 81 on שבת is also not fit for bringing a קרבן, yet she is obligated, so that cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: שבת is still a time for public offerings, but night is not
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer the שבת challenge. שבת is still fit for a קרבן צבור, but the night is not fit for any קרבן at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: No. You spoke about day 81 that falls on שבת. Even though שבת is not fit for a private offering, it is fit for a public offering. Can you say the same about a woman who miscarries on the night of day 81? The night is not fit for a private offering or for a public offering.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי defend their position against בית הלל's שבת question. They show that the שבת case and the night case are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל argued that a day can obligate a קרבן even when no קרבן can be brought that day, like שבת. בית שמאי answer that שבת is still a time when the מקדש is open for offerings, because public offerings are brought then. The night is completely closed to all offerings, so it cannot count as a 'קרבן time'.

keyTerms.meaning: A private offering brought by one person
A public offering brought for the whole community, like the daily offering
Fit or suitable (here: a fit time for bringing a קרבן)
On the night of (literally 'at the light of', meaning the evening that starts the day)
A woman who miscarries

steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread לְאוֹר as 'daytime'. Here it means the night that begins day 81.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them: No,
if you said this about the eighty-first day
that happens to fall on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָאוּי לְקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד,
phrases.english: that is because, even though it is not fit for a private offering,
it is fit for a public offering,

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּמַפֶּלֶת לְאוֹר שְׁמוֹנִים יוֹם וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: would you say the same about one who miscarries on the night of the eighty-first day,
when the night is not fit

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְקׇרְבַּן יָחִיד וְלֹא לְקׇרְבַּן צִיבּוּר?
phrases.english: neither for a private offering nor for a public offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 31 about day 81 falling on שבת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases (a 'לא, אם אמרתם' reply)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת shows that a day closed to her own קרבן can still obligate her, so night should too.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת is still a time for public offerings. Night is closed to every offering, so it is a weaker case.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sharpens the rule: what matters is whether the time is fit for offerings at all, not only for her own offering.

steps.title: Impurity does not prove a קרבן is owed
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי reject בית הלל's comparison to טומאה. A woman who miscarries before her days are complete has impure blood, but she still brings no new קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The blood does not prove anything. A woman who miscarries before her days are complete has impure blood, but she is exempt from the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי now go back to בית הלל's first argument from step 29. They knock down the proof that was based on טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל said the night of day 81 counts like the day for טומאה, so it should count for the קרבן too. בית שמאי show a case where the two do not match. A miscarriage within the counted days makes her blood טמא, yet she owes no extra קרבן. So the rules of טומאה cannot decide the rules of קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not prove the point
The completion of her counted days after birth
Impure blood
Exempt (does not have to bring it)

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי's two answers: (1) night is closed to every קרבן, unlike שבת; (2) טומאה and the duty to bring a קרבן do not always go together.

phrases.english: And the blood does not prove anything,
phrases.notes: This answers בית הלל's point in step 29, that the night is like the day when it comes to טומאה.

phrases.english: for one who miscarries before the completion of her days –
her blood is impure,
and she is exempt from the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the שבת challenge, בית שמאי go back and reject בית הלל's earlier proof from טומאה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from טומאה rules to קרבן rules.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: טומאה and the duty to bring a קרבן are separate. A miscarriage within the counted days causes טומאה but brings no new קרבן.
